lines.meet: Name's Dale, and I'll take the front and go slow. You'll get used to it, most folks do.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're out in the eastern fields too, I think. I've seen your smoke of an evening. Dale's my name.
lines.ask_home: So where'd you grow up? I always like to hear what the dirt was like.
lines.ask_work: What kind of work did you do back home? You've got the look of somebody who worked outside.
lines.answer_home: Outside Minot, North Dakota. Flat as a table, cold enough to crack a tooth in January, and I wouldn't trade it.
lines.answer_work: Wheat, two thousand acres of hard red spring. I was the fourth Brekke to farm it, and you spend the whole time waiting on weather.
lines.chat_food: My wife made a hotdish every Sunday, tater tots on top, the whole works. Folks here would think it was ish, and they'd be wrong.
lines.chat_sleep: Farmers go to bed with the sun and get up before it. I've tried sleeping in out here, and I lie there feeling guilty.
lines.chat_missing: The kids called every Sunday after church, one from Fargo and one from Denver. Sunday afternoons are long out here, you bet.
lines.chat_here: Folks keep telling me nothing'll grow in this ground. I test it everywhere I go and write it on the back of a seed packet, and something'll grow here, you bet.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're quieter than a Lutheran at a pancake breakfast, and that's saying something where I'm from.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, you could talk the bark off a fence post. Keep going, it's nice company on a long row.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you'd check the forecast three times before you'd plant a tomato. I like that in a person, you bet.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you'd cut hay in a thunderstorm. My dad would've had a word with you, and so will I one of these days.
lines.tease_any: Oh for cute, {name}, look at you. You've got mud on your boots and you didn't even wipe them.
lines.tease_back: Uff da, {name}, you got me there. I'll be chewing on that one all afternoon.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's fair, {name}. Joan would've said the same, only quicker.
lines.bristle: I'd sooner you didn't joke about that one, {name}. It's not a joking thing for me.
lines.apologise: That wasn't kind, and I'm sorry. I was raised better than that.
lines.double_down: No, I'll stand by it. My dad would have said it plainer.
lines.needle_quiet: Not a word about what's wrong, and then I find out too late. That's how you lose a crop.
lines.needle_talker: I can't hear myself think out here with you going on like that. Give it a rest a while.
lines.needle_careful: You fuss and fuss and the weather turns while you're fussing. Some things you've got to bring in when they're ready.
lines.needle_bold: You rush everything. Nothing worth having comes up quicker because you stomped on it.
lines.needle_any: You're wasteful, and you don't wipe your boots. I've noticed both, and I'm not the only one.
lines.bite_back: I've worked dirt longer than you've been alive, near enough. I'll take my time and you can mind yours.
lines.hurt: Well, okay then. I'll go back to my row and chew on that.
lines.laugh_off: Uff da, you sound like the fella at the grain elevator. He said worse every harvest and I was still there next year.
lines.confide: {name}, I farmed that land alone most of my life, and I liked it fine. Out here I find I don't like being alone near as much.
lines.listen: I hear you, {name}. Take your time, there's no rush on anything.
lines.look_out: {name}, stay behind my swing in there. I'll go slow, and you'll be fine.
lines.accept: You bet, {name}. I'll do it your way.
lines.deflect: I'm okay, {name}, don't fuss. I've been hit harder by a hailstorm.
lines.check_in: {name}, you doing all right? Sit a minute and tell me where it hurts.
lines.blame: Somebody rushed that, and the rest of us paid for it. I won't say who.
lines.thank: I thought that was me done for. Thank you, I won't forget it.
lines.brush_off: Aw, it's nothing, you'd do the same. Sit a minute and get your breath.
lines.worry: {name}, you gave me a scare there. Sit down on that rock a minute.
lines.handed_down: Pretty sure this was yours. I'll keep it like it was the combine, and you've seen me with the combine.
lines.hand_fine: Oh, you keep it, it's doing more good on you. I've got my scythe, that's plenty.
lines.hand_sulk: Somebody might've asked me first. That's all I'm going to say.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, you're good company on a long row. I mean that, you bet.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, if I ever get a field to come up clean, you're having the first loaf. That's a promise.
lines.turn_grating: We don't pull the same way, you and me. That happens, and we'll work around it.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll take the front, because it needs doing. Don't take it for anything more.
lines.make_up: I owe you an apology, {name}. I've been mule-headed, and I'm sorry for it.
lines.defend: Now that's not fair, and you know it. Leave {name} be.
lines.friend_left: Feels like an empty chair at Sunday dinner with {name} gone home a while.
lines.friend_back: Well, look who it is. Good to have you back, {name}.
lines.common_growing: I spent my whole life growing things, wheat mostly, and waiting on weather. Anybody who's farmed knows it's mostly the waiting.
lines.common_american: You're from the States? Oh for cute, where at? I'm from North Dakota, and nobody's ever heard of it.
lines.common_parent: We've got two kids, grown and gone, one to Fargo and one to Denver. They called every Sunday after church, without fail.
